checks.detail: the Matsushima-Shimobaba band limit is 0.018796 cycles per length unit against a Nyquist frequency of 0.469925, a ratio of 0.04000. Over 96.00% of the sampled band the un-band-limited kernel is undersampled and wraps energy back into the window. That is why this example exists.
checks.name: at_this_distance_the_transfer_function_needs_band_limiting

checks.detail: normalised RMS difference 6.87% between bandlimit=False and bandlimit=True. It is not a no-op, and at this z it is not a small correction either.
checks.name: band_limiting_changes_the_result_substantially

checks.detail: discrete power 0.954334 (plain ASM) -> 0.945860 (BLAS), a 0.89% reduction. The excess in the plain result is the aliased content wrapped back into the window: band limiting discards the undersampled part of the transfer function rather than synthesising anything.
checks.name: band_limiting_removes_energy_rather_than_adding_it

checks.detail: normalised RMS difference 6.87% on axis versus 9.02% with shift_yx=(0, D/2), a factor of 1.31. A displaced window samples a steeper part of the transfer function, so it is further past the band limit.
checks.name: band_limiting_matters_more_in_a_displaced_window

checks.detail: with the tilt in y, the on-axis window captures 0.4986 of the power and the y-shifted window 0.9447, a factor of 1.89. This is the y-axis counterpart of the x-axis result in c06, so the shift/tilt pairing is not an accident of one axis.
checks.name: a_y_tilt_needs_a_y_shift_to_be_recovered

demonstrates: asm_propagate(bandlimit=True|False) and its interaction with shift_yx and kykx: the Matsushima-Shimobaba band limit that keeps a long-distance angular-spectrum transfer function from aliasing.
title: Bandlimited Angular Spectrum (BLAS)
